title: The Mug Holds the Map
intro: Teal enamel beside the map; the window's wide.
A cream compass badge faces out toward the tide.
Mist holds a thin strip of ridge from my sight.
I'm Mira. We're carrying a telescope tonight.
verse1: Papa Bear, my field guide—human, patient, prepared—
Wears the rust-colored coat that helped earn him 'Bear.'
Weather, trail notice, return time—he checks.
I check torch, water, notebook, a layer for spare.
A route for each pack; if the weather turns, we turn.
My mug pins the map while my fingertip learns
The footbridge, first marker; I write down the name:
Harborlight Camp. Leave no clutter where we came.
At the entrance, I photograph the route board;
Check print against picture before walking forward.
Shortcut looks tempting; we stick to the signs.
At the overlook, that short bridge stretches its lines.
Papa shows how position can alter a view.
I label where I stood on each sketch of the two.
Level ground for the tent; keep the pathway free.
Tripod feet checked, scope cased; mug safely within reach.
chorus1: The mug holds the map, not the sky.
There's more than one angle for testing an eye.
Leave room on the page for what we can't name.
A careful look doesn't owe us a claim.
verse2: I clip down the notebook; a cloud cuts the star.
I wanted everything—there's the first limit so far.
Papa suggests that the cloud belongs in the view.
Pale sky, one bright point, water-breeze: that's true.
I lower the lantern, turn its shield to the table;
Less glare—ridge and sky grow distinct as I'm able
To find mug and page in that small amber patch.
Scope clear of the sun's last glow; full dark, then we watch.
We trade the eyepiece. Bright point; distance unknown.
Papa asks what's changed. I compare what I've shown:
Cloud moved, port lights sharpened, pale band withdrawn.
Then a streak—both looking. A moment. It's gone.
Direction, rough time; neither caught its whole flight.
No grand discovery claimed from a sliver of night.
chorus2: The mug holds the map, not the sky.
A streak doesn't give us its name passing by.
Leave room on the page for what we can't name.
A careful look doesn't owe us a claim.
verse3: Quiet together; warm mug cupped in my hands.
I write: waiting gave us what haste couldn't grant.
Before bed, route plan and notebook compared:
Sketches called sketches; uncertain stays so.
Someone absent can follow how much we could know.
Morning: mug, notebook, clip—I count before packing;
Lantern, telescope case; Papa checks for scraps lacking
A place in our packs. Nothing loose left behind.
Same marked path back, with the harbor in sight.
At the overlook, morning reshapes that same span.
A third little drawing joins where the first two began.
No eraser. Different light doesn't make those views lies.
bridge: Back at the window: teal mug, folded chart.
Four pages. Read the streak's entry apart:
An uncertain name stays uncertain in daylight.
chorus3: The mug holds the map, not the sky.
Three sketches can stand without one being a lie.
Describe what we saw before saying what it means.
No bigger story needed. Just a habit we keep.
